tools.description:
Roll the group back to the version that was live before the current one. Call lexq_groups_get first: currentVersionName is live now, previousVersionName is what a rollback restores, and a rollback is rejected while canRollback is false. A rollback needs a previous version that is still ACTIVE and whose effective end has not passed (P-058).

Pass the currentVersionId and currentDeploymentId from that call as expectedCurrentVersionId and expectedCurrentDeploymentId. If anyone deployed, rolled back or undeployed in between, the rollback is rejected with 409 and nothing changes: P-062 if another version or no version is live, P-063 if the same version is live but from a newer deployment. Read the group again and check with the user before retrying.

tools.description:

Dry runs, dry run compares, and single-decision replays share a limit of 60 evaluations per minute for each organization; a compare counts as two. Past the limit, a call fails with 429 (C-007); wait a minute before trying again.

Returns:
  inputFacts        — normalized input facts
  mutatedFacts      — input facts changed by rule actions (e.g. MUTATE_FACT mutates paymentAmount)
  generatedVariables — system-generated values; every fact in mutatedFacts gets a paired {factName}__delta key (signed difference)
  executionTraces   — per-rule match status
  decisionTraces    — per-rule decision (SELECTED / NO_MATCH / BLOCKED / etc.)

Example input: { "facts": { "paymentAmount": 100000, "customerTier": "VIP" } }

tools.description:
Create a rule in a DRAFT version. It goes last in priority order; lexq_rules_reorder changes the order.

An action's targetVar must be a registered fact (ACT-032 otherwise). Keys a rule only reads (condition fields, refVar) may stay unregistered.

Condition: { type: "SINGLE", field, operator, value, valueType } or { type: "GROUP", operator: "AND"|"OR", children: [...] }
Value types: STRING, NUMBER, BOOLEAN, LIST_STRING, LIST_NUMBER
Limits: 25 SINGLE conditions per rule (GROUP nodes do not count), 10 levels of nesting below the root, 100 rules per version.

Operators that work on each fact type:
- STRING: EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, CONTAINS (substring), IN, NOT_IN
- NUMBER: EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, GREATER_THAN, GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL, LESS_THAN, LESS_THAN_OR_EQUAL, IN, NOT_IN
- BOOLEAN: EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS
- LIST_STRING, LIST_NUMBER: HAS_ANY, HAS_ALL, HAS_NONE
IN and NOT_IN test whether the fact's value is in the array. HAS_ANY, HAS_ALL and HAS_NONE match when the fact's list holds at least one, all, or none of the array's values. The array holds values of the fact's type, or for a list fact, of its element type.
Example: { "type": "SINGLE", "field": "userTags", "operator": "HAS_ANY", "value": ["VIP","GOLD"], "valueType": "LIST_STRING" }

Actions: [{ type, parameters }]
- MUTATE_FACT: { targetVar, operator: "ASSIGN"|"ADD"|"SUB"|"MUL"|"DIV", method: "PERCENTAGE"|"AMOUNT", operand: number, refVar?, rounding? }
  Reads and writes targetVar. The request must send it (P-015 otherwise), and it must hold a number when the action runs. operand may be negative, and a percent may be over 100.
            AMOUNT                  PERCENTAGE (base = refVar, or targetVar when omitted)
    ASSIGN  targetVar = operand     targetVar = base × operand/100
    ADD     targetVar += operand    targetVar += base × operand/100
    SUB     targetVar -= operand    targetVar -= base × operand/100
    MUL     targetVar *= operand    targetVar *= (operand/100 + 1)
    DIV     targetVar /= operand    invalid
  refVar is allowed only with PERCENTAGE and ASSIGN, ADD or SUB. DIV with AMOUNT needs a nonzero operand.
  rounding: { scale: integer (0..34), mode?: "UP"|"DOWN"|"CEILING"|"FLOOR"|"HALF_UP"|"HALF_DOWN"|"HALF_EVEN" }. mode defaults to HALF_UP. Without rounding, the result keeps full precision.
- SET_FACT: { targetVar, value: string|number|boolean }. The request does not have to send targetVar.
- BLOCK: { reason? } sets isBlocked to true and blockReason to the reason, or "Policy Violation" without one. It does not stop later actions or rules; the caller enforces the block. Only BLOCK writes these two keys: a SET_FACT or MUTATE_FACT targeting either is rejected (ACT-033).

Every condition is checked against the input facts before any action runs, so a condition never sees a value an action writes in the same request. The winning rules' actions then run in priority order, each on the values the actions before it left.

tools.name: lexq_simulation_list
tools.title: List Simulations

tools.description:
Start an Impact Simulation against historical, uploaded, or inline data.

Every record a simulation processes counts toward the plan's simulation usage, including
records processed before a cancel. When the plan's limit is reached, a new simulation
cannot start.

dataset.type and dataset.source are BOTH required, and must be paired:
  HISTORICAL → source EXECUTION_LOGS, with dataset.from / dataset.to (yyyy-MM-dd, whole days
               in the organization time zone, both inclusive)
  UPLOADED   → source S3_BUCKET,      with dataset.path (the path returned by lexq_dataset_upload)
  MANUAL     → source REQUEST_BODY,   with dataset.manualData (array of fact records)

options.maxRecords: number (max 100000). When omitted, HISTORICAL and UPLOADED run at
  most 1000 records and MANUAL runs every record sent.
options.baselinePolicyVersionId: uuid (optional, for baseline comparison)
options.includeRuleStats: boolean
options.metricConfig: optional — omit for plain execution count. To aggregate a fact, pass
  { "targetVariable": "<fact>", "aggregationType": "COUNT" | "SUM" | "AVG" }

Example (uploaded dataset):
{
  "policyVersionId": "<uuid>",
  "dataset": { "type": "UPLOADED", "source": "S3_BUCKET", "path": "<path from lexq_dataset_upload>" },
  "options": { "baselinePolicyVersionId": "<uuid>", "includeRuleStats": true, "maxRecords": 10000 }
}

Example (historical):
{
  "policyVersionId": "<uuid>",
  "dataset": { "type": "HISTORICAL", "source": "EXECUTION_LOGS", "from": "2026-01-01", "to": "2026-01-31" },
  "options": { "baselinePolicyVersionId": "<uuid>", "includeRuleStats": true }
}

clearEffectiveFrom.description: Set to true to remove the effective start. Do not send effectiveFrom with it.

clearEffectiveTo.description: Set to true to remove the effective end. Do not send effectiveTo with it.

effectiveFrom.description: Effective start, ISO-8601 instant with Z or an offset, e.g. 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z or 2026-10-01T09:00:00+09:00. A bare date or a time without an offset is rejected. Omit it to keep the current start.

effectiveTo.description: Effective end, ISO-8601 instant with Z or an offset, e.g. 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z or 2026-10-01T09:00:00+09:00. A bare date or a time without an offset is rejected. Omit it to keep the current end.
